messages:
Mike: FYI I ran a combined perf + nsys trace on a 1k-token s2s workload on a Dedicated node. Seeing an unexpected CPU tail where tokenizer+scheduler take a lot more cycles compared to the baseline. uploading flame and perf samples: https://internal.gists/rw/2103344556

Eva: can you paste the perf top / flame snippet? short messages are fine. is this reproducible locally or only on Dedicated?

Mike: Reproducible on both dedicated and local dev box when using the same traffic pattern (variable seq len, bursty). Perf top (sample):
```
  30.8%  python3    [.] _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault
  12.6%  runtime    [.] schedule_batch
  8.9%   runtime    [.] tokenize_stream
  6.1%   libc.so.6  [.] memcpy
  4.5%   runtime    [.] kv_lru_maintenance
```
Full folded flame uploaded to the gist linked above.

Priya: hmm schedule_batch and tokenize_stream are big. Did kernel selection fallback to scalar kernels? nsys showed a lot of small CUDA launches around the tail. That can cause CPU churn.

Miguel: also check KV cache eviction churn: if batcher threads are thrashing the KV mutex, we'll see wakeups that inflate schedule_batch time. Try perf record with call-graph.

Mike: ran: `perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -p $PID -- sleep 30` and `perf script | flamegraph.pl > perf-kv-sched-folded.svg` The call tree shows tokenizer -> Py code -> repeated schedule_batch -> kv_lock -> pthread_cond_wait wakeups.

Eva: interesting. Two hypotheses: (1) kernel selector is picking a kernel variant that increases CPU pre/post processing for short sequences, (2) batching heuristic windowing causes many small batches -> more KV cache contention and thread wakeups.

Priya: to triage, can we run three quick experiments: A) force preferred kernel (long-seq optimized) B) disable prefetch/pipeline so there are fewer small CUDA launches C) increase batching window to accumulate tokens for 50ms and compare profiles?

Mike: I ran A + B already on a replica: forcing kernel via `RW_KERNEL_HINT=long_seq` reduced CPU tail by ~22% and reduced number of small launches in the nsys timeline. B (disable prefetch) removed a wave of short launches but increased latency P99 by ~8%.

Miguel: good. That points to kernel variant mismatch as a big contributor. Why did selector pick the other kernel? check the selector heuristics: we switch to short_seq kernel when avg_seq < 256 or when dynamic batching rate low. Maybe our seq stats are noisy due to burstiness.

Priya: I instrumented the router and pushed a quick metric: `histogram(seq_len, 1m)`. It shows bimodal with spikes under 32 and spikes ~1k. The selector looks at last_30s mean which sits ~180 -> borderline and sometimes flips.

Eva: So fallthrough to short_seq kernel during the low period causes more CPU overhead for the long requests that arrive simultaneously. Two mitigation ideas: - make selector use percentiles (95th) not mean, or - prefer the kernel with lower CPU pre/post cost when variance high.

Mike: I'm for percentile-based rule. Quick experiment: changed selector to check `p95(seq_len) > 400 -> force long_seq` and redeployed on a staging replica. Perf flame after change: top CPU frame from schedule_batch dropped 18% and tokenize_stream dropped 12%. nsys timeline shows fewer tiny launches and longer, coalesced kernels.

Miguel: nice. Any KV cache effects left? the perf samples still show some kv_lru_maintenance hits. Could be background compaction triggered more often due to prefetch disabled earlier.

Priya: For KV we should: 1) add per-batch KV hit/miss counters, 2) avoid doing LRU maintenance on the hot path (move to background thread with bounded budget), 3) measure mutex contention via `perf lock` and `trace_event` instrumentation.

Mike: I ran `perf lock record` for 60s and saw spikes where kv mutex contended for ~2-4ms at 200Hz during bursts. Pushing a variant that offloads LRU maintenance to `kv_maintenance_thread` (budgeted) shows lock hold time reduced by ~70% in perf summary.

Eva: Great. Action items?

Priya: 1) merge kernel selector p95 change behind a feature flag (cc @Miguel for review) 2) roll KV maintenance off to background thread with budget and add metrics 3) run 48h soak to validate P99 and cost impact (both perf and nsys traces) 4) add unit test for selector with synthetic bimodal seq distributions.

Miguel: I'll review selector PR. Also add a short perf benchmarking harness that can replay bursty traces (we need deterministic replay to compare kernel variants).

perf-bot: automated test results for `kernel-selector-p95` on staging: perf regression check: CPU tokens/unit -3.4% (improved), P99 latency +0.9% (within threshold).

Mike: thanks all. I'll open the PRs and link perf/nvsys artifacts here. tagging follow-up: @Priya to own KV change, @Miguel to own selector rollout, @Eva to own soak plan.

Eva: ack. let's reconvene after the 48h soak and share the perfetto timelines. :thumbsup:
